text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Meningoencephalitis (likely Herpes Simplex Virus).

Your symptoms of fever, altered mentation, confusion, and generalized rigidity strongly suggest an infectious process involving the brain and meninges. I have already requested a CT Head and CSF analysis to confirm the diagnosis and identify the specific pathogen.
